note: Honest coverage frontier. status: present = a runnable godog step drives real code and passes (must name a test); pending = specified behavior whose implementation does not exist yet. Two scenarios are pending because the reporting work they assert (the zero-numerator bound) is not yet implemented — declared rather than papered over (INV-22).

scenarios.name: Every measurement surface is bound to this spec in the lockstep lock
The measurement SQL is covered by a golden fixture whose expected values are hand-computed
A perturbed axis query turns its golden test red
An axis that excludes unmeasurable rows reports the exclusion
A zero-numerator axis is published with its upper bound
scenarios.note: The rule was implemented as a closure inside cmd/axisscore's text renderer, so nothing could execute it and nothing else could reuse it. Extracted to core/axis.ZeroNumeratorBound (+ the numeric ZeroNumeratorUpperBound for gauge callers) and driven by four oracles: the bare-zero refusal, the bound shrinking with n (the property a bare zero hides), the empty-sample vacuity floor in BOTH the string and numeric forms, and the worked example 0-of-12 = 22.1% (the exact one-sided Clopper–Pearson limit since TG-670; the rule-of-three 3/n it replaced printed 150% for 0 of 2).
